binders: For every natural number m with 0<m, let V be the real vector space of functions from {0,…,m−1} to R.
For every grid with endpoint functions L,R: Z→R satisfying L_i<R_i and R_{i−1}=L_i for every integer i.
For every q: R→R→V, where the first argument is spatial position and the second is time, and every flux: V→V satisfying the integral conservation hypothesis.
For every rule: R→R→(Z→V)→Z→V, assigning edge vectors from two times and an entire old cell-state function.
For every pair of real times s,t with s<t and every old: Z→V.

The cell conclusions hold for every integer i. Within the last conclusion, oldBound, leftBound, and rightBound are universally quantified real numbers, independently for that cell and the preceding data.
hypotheses: The grid contains proofs that L_i<R_i and R_{i−1}=L_i for every i∈Z.
For every real a,b,u, the function x↦q(x,u) is interval integrable from a to b with respect to Lebesgue measure.
For every real x,a,b, the function τ↦flux(q(x,τ)) is interval integrable from a to b with respect to Lebesgue measure.
For all real a,b,u,v, ∫_a^b q(x,v) dx − ∫_a^b q(x,u) dx = ∫_u^v [flux(q(a,τ)) − flux(q(b,τ))] dτ, with oriented vector-valued interval integrals.
Only within the final conditional estimate: ||old_i−Q_i(s)||∞≤oldBound, ||F_i−G_i||∞≤leftBound, and ||F_{i+1}−G_{i+1}||∞≤rightBound.
conclusions: The proposition concludes 0<m again, together with all the following statements for every i∈Z.
L_i<R_i, x↦q(x,s) is interval integrable from L_i to R_i, and Q_i(s) equals (R_i−L_i)⁻¹∫_{L_i}^{R_i} q(x,s) dx.
L_i<R_i, x↦q(x,t) is interval integrable from L_i to R_i, and Q_i(t) equals (R_i−L_i)⁻¹∫_{L_i}^{R_i} q(x,t) dx.
s<t, τ↦flux(q(L_i,τ)) is interval integrable from s to t, and G_i=(t−s)⁻¹∫_s^t flux(q(L_i,τ)) dτ.
For every real oldBound,leftBound,rightBound satisfying the three error-bound hypotheses, ||U_i−Q_i(t)||∞≤oldBound+(Δt/h_i)(leftBound+rightBound).
mathematical_definitions: V=R^{Fin m} has pointwise addition, subtraction, and real scalar multiplication. Its norm is ||v||∞=max_{0≤k<m}|v_k|.
Write L_i=grid.cellLeft(i), R_i=grid.cellRight(i), and h_i=R_i−L_i>0. Adjacency also gives R_i=L_{i+1}.
For a V-valued function f, its normalized interval integral is A(f;a,b)=(b−a)⁻¹∫_a^b f(x) dx.
An interval-average certificate for f,a,b,z means a<b, interval integrability of f from a to b, and z=A(f;a,b).
Q_i(u)=A(x↦q(x,u);L_i,R_i) is the exact spatial cell average at time u.
F_j=rule(s,t,old)(j) is the selected numerical edge vector. G_j=A(τ↦flux(q(L_j,τ));s,t) is the exact time-averaged physical flux at the left endpoint of cell j.
For Lebesgue measure λ, M(S,f)=((λ(S)).toReal)⁻¹∫_S f dλ. On the target intervals, the denominators are respectively h_i and Δt.
The oriented integral ∫_a^b f dλ is ∫_(a,b] f dλ−∫_(b,a] f dλ. Interval integrability requires integrability on both sets.
All vector equalities hold in every component. There are no existential witnesses: the averages, flux averages, and updated states are fixed by definitions.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every positive finite number of real components, every integer-indexed grid of positive-width adjacent cells, and every state field and state-to-flux map satisfying slice integrability and the integral conservation identity on every real space-time rectangle, choose any numerical edge rule, any forward time interval, and any old cell-state function. Then the exact cell averages at both times and the exact time-averaged left-edge fluxes satisfy their positive-interval integrability and normalized-integral specifications. The initial cell average and the exact edge flux also equal the corresponding normalized half-open-set integrals. The update is the old state minus the elapsed-time-to-cell-width ratio times the right numerical flux minus the left numerical flux. Its cell-width-weighted error against the exact final average equals the cell-width-weighted initial error plus elapsed time times the left flux error minus the right flux error. Consequently, any bounds on the initial cell error and the two neighboring flux errors give an updated maximum-component-norm error bound equal to the initial bound plus the elapsed-time-to-width ratio times the sum of the two flux bounds. All these conclusions hold simultaneously for every integer cell, and the positive component count is repeated as a conclusion.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The state space is a positive finite product of real scalar components, with maximum-component norm. The target does not quantify over arbitrary normed spaces or arbitrary norms.

The grid is indexed by all integers, has strictly positive widths, and has exactly matching adjacent endpoints. It need not be uniform, have widths bounded above or below, or cover the entire real line.
The assumption on q and flux is global in all real spatial endpoints and times. The theorem does not establish existence or uniqueness of a field satisfying it.
The integral conservation identity is assumed directly. No differentiability, pointwise differential equation, entropy condition, or separate continuity assumption on flux is encoded.
The numerical rule and old state are arbitrary. No consistency, locality, monotonicity, positivity, stability condition, time-step restriction, or convergence rate is assumed or concluded.
No closeness of old to the exact initial averages is assumed outside the final conditional estimate. No smallness of numerical flux errors is established.
The bounds are arbitrary real numbers. Their premises force them to be nonnegative; if any premise fails, that instance of the estimate is vacuous.
The positive component count excludes an empty component index type. Positive cell widths and s<t exclude zero denominators and empty target averaging intervals.

The average definitions use totalized real inversion and a real conversion of extended measure. Such definitions can degenerate for zero or infinite measure, but all regions used here have strictly positive finite Lebesgue measure.
The result is a per-cell, single-step identity and conditional error estimate. It does not assert a sum over all cells, a bound uniform in the cell index, or a multi-step error estimate.
The explicit set-average equality for spatial averages is stated at s only. The final-time average is certified through its normalized interval integral.
Exact edge fluxes use values q(L_j,τ) at the specified spatial points. No independent trace operator or boundary-value selection is encoded.
